You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Clinical history (case record; may contain prior observations):
age: 11
gender: male
history: An 11-year-old male child came with a 4-day history of fever, vomiting, abdominal pain, and a recent bout of cough with expectoration. A past history of congenital stridor, which was subsequently diagnosed as laryngomalacia, was managed conservatively. Since then, the child has had frequent hospitalisations due to recurrent lung infections.

Based on the chest radiograph findings described in Figure 1, and considering the clinical history of recurrent lung infections and laryngomalacia, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A) Congenital lobar overinflation  
B) Unilateral absence of main pulmonary artery  
C) Bullous emphysema  
D) Hypogenetic lung syndrome  
E) Swyer–James–MacLeod syndrome  
F) Poland syndrome
